orlando-steam-league.summary: Students design a space colony while working across five theme parks, NASA's Kennedy Space Center and the UCF campus, where they spend two full academic days.

pathway.S: Coding at the Digital Hub and the physics behind Disney's Hollywood Studios
pathway.T: Six-degrees-of-freedom workshop at Universal and robotics with Ozobots
pathway.E: Environmental engineering at Epic Universe and a coaster design inspired by VelociCoaster (Islands of Adventure)
pathway.A: Art of Animation: colony layout and space-suit design

visits: Two academic days on the UCF campus
inclusions: Meals during the academic program (except three meals)
Software and materials (students bring their own laptop)
orlando-steam-league.rooms: Gender-split rooms of 2–4 students (up to 5 in suites). 10 pm curfew.

diary.title: Touchdown in Orlando
diary.body: Customised backpacks, new faces and the first team-ups.

diary.title: Campus, then studios
diary.body: Learning at the university in the morning, Disney’s Hollywood Studios in the afternoon.

diary.title: Engineering meets adventure
diary.body: The science behind how vehicles move, then seeing it in action on the Transformers ride at Universal.

diary.title: On stage at NASA
diary.body: After days of building and refining, students present their own projects at NASA.

europe-steam-league.summary: Twelve days in the UK building a digital STEAM career portfolio, based on the Woldingham School campus with an excursion to Oxford.
visits: Red Bull Racing behind the scenes
inclusions: The Lion King and Arsenal Stadium tickets

steam-league-ai.summary: An artificial-intelligence innovation studio at Bradfield College, with projects aligned to the Sustainable Development Goals.

tokyo-steam-championship.tagline: Building Solutions for Better Cities and Communities
tokyo-steam-championship.summary: The top 20 winning schools from past leagues prepare for six months and present solutions for better cities and communities in Tokyo. Held every two years; the winning team gets a cash prize and Coded's support to implement its project.

faq.title: FAQ
faq.metaDescription: Ages, enrollment, pricing, forms, health, accommodation and what each Coded program includes.
faq.intro: Can't find your answer? Book a call and we'll help.
faq.askBody: We'll answer on a short call or by email.

items.q: What ages are the programs for?
What English level do students need?
items.a: B1 (intermediate) or higher, for every program.
Students are grouped by age into Junior and Senior, in mixed-level classes.
Yes, when they complete their project.

items.q: Can a student join without their school?
items.a: Yes, through World Citizens. Every student has a personal Guardian, and there is one chat group for students and another for parents.

items.q: How much does a program cost?
items.a: Ask us about pricing: on a call we'll go through the cost of each program and the payment options.
Register online, choose your dates and pay the enrollment fee by card. Installment plans are available, and Klarna where available.

items.q: Which forms do we need to fill in?
items.a: In the Parent Portal: medical form, T-shirt size, media release and pick-up authorization.
In Orlando, in gender-split rooms of 2 to 4 students (up to 5 in suites). In the UK, in private-college dorms. Access is by passcode or keypass, with staff on site 24/7.

items.q: How do families know how things are going?
items.a: Each student's Guardian shares updates and photos with the family every day.

items.q: What if a student needs medical care?
items.a: There is an on-site doctor, health insurance and arrangements with local healthcare providers.
For Orlando STEAM League, yes: each student brings their own laptop.

items.q: How do schools reach the Tokyo STEAM Championship?
items.a: The 20 winning schools from past leagues prepare for six months and present their project in Tokyo. It is held every two years.

method.title: Our method
method.metaDescription: The Coded method: experts, live workshops, project-based learning and coding, building skills that open careers.
method.intro: Four steps take every student from the classroom to the project: they learn from experts, practise in live workshops, build a real solution and code it.

creativity.body: Using arts to think in new and innovative ways.
creativity.careers: Data Scientist, Virtual Reality Designer, Bioengineer and more.

collaboration.careers: Climate Change Analyst, Doctor, Teacher, Journalist, Social Media Manager and more.

adaptability.body: STEAM projects often require students to adjust their methods as they encounter new challenges.
adaptability.careers: Electrician, Chef, Mechanical Engineer, Nurse, Lawyer and more.

problemSolving.body: Tackling challenges using science, math and technology.
problemSolving.careers: Architect, Designer, Civil Engineer, Accountant, Operations Manager, Pharmacist, Supply Chain Manager and more.

technical.careers: Software Developer, Drone Manager, 3D Printing Specialist, AI Ethicist, Web Developer, IT Support Specialist and more.

criticalThinking.careers: Real Estate Agent, Cybersecurity Analyst, Mechanical Engineer, HR Manager, Psychologist, Pilot, Veterinarian, Dentist and more.

method.groupsBody: Students are grouped by age into Junior and Senior, in mixed-level classes, and receive a certificate when they complete their project.
